hook.line: The year “CHAIN SHOT” appeared for Japanese home computers — the ancestor of the tile-clearing puzzle the world knows as SameGame.
hook.say: Clearing big clumps of one colour feels great!

ch.t: From a magazine to the world
ch.say: It started in a Japanese computer magazine.
p: In 1985 Kuniaki Moribe made “CHAIN SHOT” for the Fujitsu FM-8/FM-7; it was published through the magazine Gekkan ASCII.
Eiji Fukumoto’s 1992 Unix version, “SameGame”, gave it its lasting name, and ports and remakes followed worldwide.
st: Eiji Fukumoto’s Unix SameGame fixes the name
Jawbreaker spreads it on handheld devices

tl: A Windows 3.1 version, with an English edition

ch.t: The bigger the clump, the higher the score
ch.say: The trick is to grow big clumps!
ch.cap: Clear a group of one colour and the blocks above fall down
p: Just remove two or more touching blocks of the same colour.
Bigger groups score far more, so planning the order of removal is everything.
